resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1975 for the present enclosed tower. A 1933 newspaper item describes a CCC-built 18-foot tower and lookout house, and a 1948 survey describes a 20-foot enclosed wooden tower. No source says whether the 1975 tower replaced the 1948 structure directly. The record keeps 1975 for the present tower and adds the earlier structures as events.

The register says the lookout has been occasionally staffed by US Forest Service personnel. The 2006 photo note says it is often staffed in fire season by the state forestry agency. Both are reported with their dates, and no current staffing status is confirmed.
The register gives 5,835 ft (1,779 m) and PeakBagging gives 5,831 ft. The brief's 1,778.5 m is kept; no elevation appears in the story.

notes_for_editor: Only three sources were read. The most recent staffing and condition evidence is the 2019 register entry and a 2006 photo note, so current staffing and access are not confirmed. Access level is omitted; the only access fact is the register's 'some 6 miles from paved road'. Several Bear Mountain lookouts exist (Fresno County, Shasta-Bear with ALERTCalifornia cameras, Fowler, Siskiyou). This record was matched to the Siskiyou station by county, coordinates and the PeakBagging Siskiyou County entry; the 1939 Dry creek fire item on the weebly bear-mountain1.html page was not used because it is not confirmed to be this station. The register credits photos (Ron Kemnow 2008, Fred Johnson 2006) with no direct image URLs captured, so no photos entry was added.
